name: Rabeprazole
summary: Activates non-enzymatically, so its effect is fast and far less dependent on a patient’s CYP2C19 genotype than the other PPIs.
good: Rapid symptom control on day one, or when CYP2C19 polymorphism makes other PPIs unpredictable.
bad: Less widely stocked/genericized in some markets than omeprazole, which can be a practical (not pharmacologic) limitation.
clinicalPearls: If a patient needs relief starting the same day rather than by the end of the week, rabeprazole’s non-enzymatic activation is the mechanistic reason to pick it.
mechanism: H⁺/K⁺-ATPase inhibition after conversion to its active sulfenamide — but the conversion is largely acid-catalyzed rather than CYP-catalyzed.
pharmacodynamics: Strong, consistent pH >4 control; often cited as the most genotype-independent of the older PPIs.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Fastest first-dose effect among the classic PPIs — meaningful acid suppression is often seen after just one dose.
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Largely non-enzymatic activation; minor CYP2C19/3A4 involvement in subsequent clearance only.

indications: GERD, duodenal ulcer, H. pylori eradication.
interactionNotes: Fewer genotype-driven variability issues than omeprazole/lansoprazole; still carries the general PPI absorption-interaction cautions (iron, azoles, atazanavir).
